transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-06-10
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Cho (Redwood SE), Amir Novak (Redwood), Maya Thompson (CTO - Horizon), Carlos Ruiz (Head of Infra), Priya Shah (Security), Ben Carter (ML Eng)

Summary: quick scoping session for a POC focusing on private networking and data residency. We walked through options: VPC peering vs PrivateLink, regional constraints (EU residency), egress limitations and auditability. Some transcription noise and a few mis-heard product names (Redwood products referred to as redwood ded/priv, sometimes "Redwood Dedicated" said as ded or dedcap).

00:00:03 - Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Samir from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. Quick intros and then we'll jump into the network and residency constraints.
00:00:18 - Maya: Thanks, Samir. I'm Maya, CTO at Horizon. We have Carlos and Priya here for infra and security, and Ben for ML. High level, we need a private deployment for PHI workloads, EU data residency and strict egress controls.
00:00:35 - Samir: Great, that's exactly what we're here to scope. Lena, want to run through the options?
00:00:40 - Lena: Sure, thanks. So for private networking we typically propose two patterns: VPC peering (straight peering between our VPC in your cloud account and Redwood's dedicated VPC) or PrivateLink/Private Endpoint style where traffic goes over AWS PrivateLink or Azure Private Endpoint. The tradeoffs - peering tends to be simpler for bidirectional access, PrivateLink limits inbound connections and is a bit more controlled for egress.
00:01:05 - Carlos: Quick q - with peering, do we have to open any public IP egress at all? Our compliance team wants zero public egress for certain datasets.
00:01:13 - Lena: For the peering flow, traffic stays on the cloud backbone - there should be no public egress for inference requests if you route them through the peered subnets and route tables. The only exception is if you need telemetry or metrics to reach external monitoring endpoints; those can be configured via VPC endpoints or logging collectors inside your network.
00:01:35 - Priya: And for PrivateLink? We prefer PrivateLink generally because it avoids cross-account routing tables, but we need to confirm cross-region support for our EU clusters.
00:01:44 - Lena: PrivateLink works per region; you would need an endpoint in the same region as your clients. If you have EU residency requirements, we can stand up endpoints in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 or use our Private deployment in your VPC in that region.
00:02:00 - Ben: Are there latency implications? We're running some latency sensitive features - p95 under 200ms for single-turn completion ideally.
00:02:07 - Samir: Good question. For p95 under 200ms, model selection, sequence lengths, and the network hop matter. With dedicated peering inside the same region and GPU-backed instances, it's realistic for shorter prompts and smaller models. For larger models and longer contexts, you should expect higher tail latency. We'll benchmark.
00:02:26 - Maya: Our success criteria for the POC: 1) Data never leaves EU for EU-tagged records, 2) p95 latency < 250ms for our median prompt set at 4 concurrent users, 3) throughput >= 60 requests/minute sustained, and 4) verifiable audit logs of requests (token-level not required but request success/failure and timestamps).
00:02:50 - Samir: Perfect, that's clear. We'll capture those as the POC success criteria.
00:02:55 - Carlos: For workload sizing - rough numbers: peak 10 qps per region, expected burst up to 25 qps for short windows, concurrent sessions typically 6-8. Token lengths average 150 tokens per request.
00:03:09 - Ben: Also, some reranking jobs will send 10-20 candidates, so those are multiply heavier. We should consider batching.
00:03:18 - Lena: Right, we'll recommend batching and possibly a smaller quantized model variant for reranking. For sizing, based on 150 tokens and 10 qps, that maps to roughly X tokens/sec - we'll send an initial sizing calc.
00:03:30 - Samir: To be concrete, our POC benchmark will include: (a) a 1-hour sustained run at your median qps (10 qps), (b) a 5-minute spike test to 25 qps, (c) a set of 200 reranking requests with 10 candidates, and (d) verification of request routing and audit logs. We'll measure p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, and error rates.
00:03:50 - Priya: For auditability, we need immutable logs, SAML SSO for the console, SOC2 attestation or similar. Do you have SOC2 Type II?
00:04:00 - Samir: Yes, we have SOC2 Type II. We'll share the security pack and the SOC2 report under an NDA. For logs, we can stream audit logs to your S3 or Splunk via a private network path.
00:04:12 - Priya: KMS integration? Keys must be in our account.
00:04:16 - Lena: We support customer-managed keys (CMK) via AWS KMS or Azure Key Vault for the control plane; for private deployments we can ensure keys remain in your HSM/KMS. We'll include a KMS integration playbook.
00:04:29 - Maya: Region-wise, EU residency is critical. If we run model inference in eu-West-1 that's acceptable; what about fallback if capacity saturated? We need no fallback to US.
00:04:40 - Samir: Understood - we'll lock routing policy for the POC to EU-only model replicas and fallbacks within EU regions. We'll document the routing policy and fail closed rather than falling back to hosted US models.
00:04:55 - Carlos: On networking ports and firewall rules, what do we need to open?
00:04:59 - Lena: Primarily outbound TLS (443) to specific internal IP ranges if using PrivateLink; with peering you'll route to our endpoint IPs in the peered VPC - we'll provide a port list but typically it's 443 for the API endpoints plus a few ports for metrics if you choose push. We also support VPC endpoints for S3 flow logs.
00:05:18 - Ben: For benchmarks, will you run them from our infra or from Redwood?
00:05:22 - Samir: Prefer to run them from within your network for the most realistic network measurements. We'll provide a lightweight runner (python script) you can execute in a bastion or CI job; it will produce p50/p95/p99 and token metrics. If that's not possible we can run from Redwood's peered environment but we'll note the difference.
00:05:40 - Maya: We'll run the runner from our test infra. Expect some initial network windows - best effort to schedule next Wednesday morning.
00:05:47 - Lena: Great. For the runner we'll need a short-lived API key and an IP allowlist for the test window, or if using PrivateLink no public key exposure is required. We'll include options.
00:05:58 - Carlos: Egress constraints: some of our data is strictly non-export - can Redwood promise no model weights or backups leave region?
00:06:07 - Samir: For the private deployment we can guarantee that model inference and storage remain in-region; we will not replicate logs outside the region unless requested. We'll document data residency and provide an SLA clause for the POC.
00:06:20 - Priya: We need encryption in transit and at rest, and access controls with RBAC integrated to our SSO.
00:06:26 - Lena: Supported. We'll include the RBAC role mapping and SSO SAML config.
00:06:31 - Samir: Timeline - recommended pilot: 4-6 weeks. Week 0: setup and network configuration, Week 1: run initial benchmark, Week 2: tuning/quantization experiments and reranking, Week 3-4: validation and security sign-off. We can compress if you have tight deadlines.
00:06:49 - Maya: We're targeting a production decision by mid-July, so a 4-week POC starting next week fits.
00:06:56 - Samir: Okay, next steps recap then: I'll send pricing and SOW, Lena will send the network diagram and firewall rules, Ben will send prompt corpus, Priya will send the compliance checklist. We'll schedule the tech deep dive with Carlos and Ben. We'll aim to start network work Monday 2027-06-14.
00:07:12 - Carlos: One more nit: can you provide sample benchmark numbers for a similar customer? Just ballpark - gives infra team comfort.
00:07:19 - Lena: We can share anonymized benchmarks - e.g., for a 13B quantized model in eu-west-1 we typically see p95 ~ 120-200ms for short prompts, tokens/sec around 800-1200 depending on batching. We'll send a benchmark spreadsheet with more detail.
00:07:37 - Ben: Good. For reranking we'll want to experiment with batch size 8/16 and maybe a smaller 6B quantized variant to reduce cost.
00:07:45 - Samir: Noted. Any blockers on compliance for the SSO or SOC2 docs before we can share the SOC2?
00:07:52 - Priya: NDA in place? We have a mutual NDA with your legal team, yes. We'll confirm with legal but we can accept SOC2 under NDA.
00:08:00 - Samir: Great.
00:08:03 - Maya: Alright that's it from me, thanks.
00:08:05 - Samir: Thanks everyone. I'll follow up with the notes and the artifacts.

End of meeting.

Artifacts & Links:
- Preliminary network diagram (to be attached)
- Benchmark runner repo: github.com/redwood-inference/bench-runner (note: link spoken, may be referenced in follow-up)
- Security pack (SOC2, KMS guides) to be shared under NDA

POC Success Criteria (recap):
- Data residency: EU-only for EU-tagged data, no fallback to US
- Performance: p95 < 250ms for median prompt set at target concurrency
- Throughput: sustain >= 60 req/min (aligns with peak qps numbers)
- Auditability: exportable audit logs to customer's S3/Splunk over private link

Benchmark plan (recap):
- 1-hour sustained run at median qps (10 qps)
- 5-minute spike to 25 qps
- 200 reranking requests with 10 candidates each
- Collect p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, error rate, and network hop latency

Timeline (recap):
- Start: week of 2027-06-14 (network setup)
- Initial benchmark: within 1 week of start
- Tuning & reranking experiments: week 2
- Security validation & sign-off: week 3-4
- Decision target: mid-July 2027

Caveats / Notes:
- Some speaker labels may be slightly off in the transcript; product names referred informally ("ded" for Dedicated, "priv" for Private).
- We'll share anonymized benchmarks and a sizing spreadsheet before the runner run.
